The starter kit

Everything in this guide is built into files you can start from, so the right answer is the default answer.

Every color, font size and chart constant comes from one file, tokens/tokens.json. Change it there, run the build, and every template, theme and this guide update together.

Pin these two. The cheat sheet and the chart chooser are pages of this guide (top bar), and print as one-page PDFs.

Toolkit

Set up once

For decks and workbooks, most people need to install nothing: start from the template and copy charts from the starter deck.

Everything named here is in the kit: the release bundle (a zip on SharePoint) or the GitHub repo. More detail and troubleshooting:

  • docs/office-setup.md
  • docs/powerbi-setup.md
  • AGENTS.md (Python, HTML, R)
Check the font

In PowerPoint, type Libre Franklin in the font box. If it's listed, you're set. If not, open the kit's fonts folder, select every file, right-click › Install (or ask IT).

PowerPoint

New deck: File › New › the McKesson Standard Template. Charts: open the kit's starter deck, copy a chart slide into your deck, then right-click the chart › Edit Data and paste your numbers. Colors, fonts and layout come with the slide.

Excel

Open the kit's chart workbook: replace a sheet's data, or copy its chart into your file. The Palette sheet lists every color with the hex to type into More Colors. Want the colors in your own workbooks? The optional theme files are in office-setup.

Power BI

View › Themes › Browse for themes and pick dist/powerbi/mckesson-dataviz-theme.json. Viewers without Libre Franklin see Segoe UI, so leave room in labels.

Python
$kit = "git+https://github.com/amccown-mck/Data-Viz-Guide@v1.1.0#subdirectory=python"
pip install "mckviz @ $kit"     # fonts and maps included
import mckviz as mv
mv.use()          # fonts, matplotlib style, Plotly template "mck"
C = mv.colors     # C.focus, C.context, C.accent, C.negative ...
HTML

Link dist/web/mck-viz.css for the CSS variables and chart-card styles; add mck-plotly-template.js for Plotly or use vega-lite-config.json as the Vega-Lite config. Start from templates/html/chart-card.html.

R

source("dist/r/theme_mck.R"), then ff <- mck_font() and theme_mck(base_family = ff). Render with ragg.

Toolkit

Check before you send

Run this list on every chart that leaves the team, whoever or whatever made it.

In Python, mv.lint(fig) checks the mechanical items for you: titles and source present, at most six colors, palette only (amber is an error), no red–green, bars from zero, labels versus axis, legends, dual axes, pies, rotated or tiny text. It also reminds you to check any orange carries meaning.

No tool can tell whether the headline is true or the chart fits the question. That part needs a person, or an agent told to check.

Rendered from docs/qa-checklist.md, so it always matches.

Message

  • Headline is a full-sentence insight, ≤ 2 lines, no final period, balanced line breaks.
  • Every claim in the headline is visibly supported (recompute counts, multipliers, "all/most/none").
  • Subtitle states metric, unit, scope and period, and nothing opinionated.
  • The chart type matches the question (choosing-a-chart.md).
  • One message per chart; ≤ 2 charts per slide.

Color and emphasis

  • Highlight follows the headline: grey context, blue focus, navy accent; ≤ 2 highlighted items. Orange appears only where something is worse (negative, below target).
  • Categorical colors (if any) come from the fixed order, ≤ 6, consistent across the deck.
  • No red–green contrasts; nothing encoded by color alone.
  • Focus category labels are bolded/colored to echo the highlight.

Data integrity

  • Bars/columns start at zero (waterfall exception is marked and footnoted).
  • Bubble area ∝ value; pie/donut sums to 100% and has ≤ 5 segments.
  • No dual axes (or justified and clearly labelled).
  • Sorted by value, or in a natural order (time, bands, levels).
  • Small multiples share a scale.
  • Numbers rounded sensibly; units in subtitle; true minus (−); consistent K/M/B.

Clutter

  • Direct labels instead of a legend where possible; legend (if any) top-left, in data order.
  • No borders, 3D, shadows, gradients, heavy gridlines, tick marks, rotated axis titles.
  • Value axis removed when values are labelled.
  • Nothing overlaps: labels, callouts, legend, headline, reference lines.

Typography and layout

  • Libre Franklin (or approved fallback); role sizes per typography-and-layout.md; nothing below 9 pt / 11 px.
  • Headline, subtitle, key, footnote and source share one left edge.
  • Sentence case; consistent terminology (FTE vs. headcount; fiscal vs. calendar year).

Source and ethics

  • Footnotes define metrics and caveats.
  • Source line names the system(s), as-of date and population.
  • No group smaller than the minimum n (default 10), including in tooltips, filters and drill-downs.
  • Protected attributes used only for approved analyses, aggregated.
  • Forecasts/estimates are labelled and show a range or scenario.

Accessibility and delivery

  • Text contrast ≥ 4.5:1; fills < 3:1 carry labels.
  • Alt text / text summary provided (headline + key numbers).
  • Right format: native Office chart, SVG/PDF or 300 dpi PNG for print, 200 dpi PNG for screens, or responsive HTML.
  • Mobile/dark variants checked if the chart will be shown that way.

For coding agents

Claude, Copilot and other agents follow the same rules as people, automatically.

In this repo, agents read AGENTS.md on their own (Claude through CLAUDE.md, Copilot through .github/copilot-instructions.md, plus per-language rules for Python, web and R files).

In any other repo, copy one file: dist/agents/mck-viz-rules.md. It is generated from the tokens, so its colors are always current.

Ask for a chart like this

"Make a McKesson chart of voluntary attrition by job family for FY26 from examples/data/attrition_by_job_family.csv, for a leadership deck. Highlight the families above the enterprise rate."

What comes back

The mck-chart skill walks the five steps (question, chart type, build, headline, QA), runs mv.lint, looks at the rendered chart, and returns the file, a chart brief and alt text.

The chart brief

Question:    Where is attrition concentrated?
Mode:        explanatory     Medium: slide
Chart:       sorted bar (cookbook/bar.md)
Focus:       2 families > enterprise rate
Headline:    Two frontline job families lose
             about 1 in 4 people a year ...
Subtitle:    Voluntary attrition by job
             family, FY26 (%)
Source:      Workday HCM (synthetic), 31 Mar 2026
Min n check: smallest group 700 (>= 10)
QA:          pass
